Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side, or if it's something in our integration? We can share logs — attaching a short sample.

Thanks,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-18 09:47 -07:00
Subject: [INCIDENT] Aegis-2.7B elevated 5xx - initial triage

TL;DR: Root cause appears to be an interaction between a new kernel selection heuristic and long-sequence KV cache growth for Aegis-2.7B that caused excessive memory pressure on a subset of GPU hosts, triggering request rejections (5xx) and timeouts.

Details:
- Observed spike: 08:35-09:05 PST, error rate up to 20% on a specific shard group (us-west-2-prod-shard-12).
- Repro: synthetic load against Aegis-2.7B with sequences >6k tokens caused similar queue growth on shard-12.
- Immediate mitigation applied at 09:05: rolling fallback of shard-12 to the previous kernel selection path + temporary request rate cap for long-sequence requests. Error rate dropped to <0.5% by 09:12.

Next actions:
1) Full host sweep to validate no residual memory leak (ETA 3 hours).
2) Revert new heuristic for Aegis-2.7B globally until a fix lands (ETA 24h).
3) Postmortem and customer communication draft.

I'll follow up with logs and a brief postmortem draft for Marissa to share.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-09-18 10:20 -07:00
Subject: Aegis-2.7B incident update — mitigation applied and next steps

Jamie / Ava —

Quick update from the triage: engineering identified a kernel selection heuristic interaction that increased memory pressure on a subset of hosts serving Aegis-2.7B for long-context workloads. We rolled back the heuristic on the impacted shard and applied a short-term rate cap for very long sequences. The visible error rate returned to baseline by ~09:12 PST.

What this means for Starlite: your traffic should be back to normal. We will:
- Conduct a full validation sweep of the affected hosts (in progress).
- Revert the heuristic globally only after patch verification and additional automated checks (target: 24 hours).
- Share a concise postmortem and proposed compensatory credit (applied to your next invoice).

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf (draft), rollback-timeline.csv (internal timeline)

Would you like a short sync (15 min) this afternoon to walk through the timeline and answer questions?

Best,
Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie@starlite.com>, Ava Reed <ava.reed@starlite.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-21 16:42 -07:00
Subject: Aegis-2.7B postmortem and follow-up items

Hi Jamie / Ava —

Thanks again for your patience last week. We've completed the internal postmortem and validation sweep. Summary and actions below; full draft is attached.

Summary:
- Root cause: an opt-in kernel-selection heuristic intended to reduce per-token latency for medium-length sequences interacted poorly with Aegis-2.7B's KV cache growth for long-context requests, producing sustained memory pressure on a small set of GPU hosts and triggering request rejections (5xx) and timeouts.
- Impact window: 2028-09-18 08:35–09:12 PST (peak error rate ~20%).
- Customers affected: small percentage of traffic routed to the impacted shard; Starlite saw ~18% error rate during the peak window.

Remediation and safeguards implemented:
1) Immediate rollback of the heuristic on affected shards at 09:05 PST (complete).
2) Global disable of the heuristic for Aegis-2.7B until a robust memory-aware version ships (completed 2028-09-18 18:00 PST).
3) Enhanced host-level memory pressure monitoring + an automated request-shed policy for long sequences (deployed 2028-09-20).
4) A canary evaluation for all future kernel changes focused on long-context models (process change).

Compensation: We've applied a one-time service credit equal to 10% of Starlite's usage for the affected billing period; details attached and visible on your account billing page.

Follow-ups we recommend on your side: pin critical production routes to the stable variant (Aegis-2.7B:stable) for the next 72 hours if you'd like a conservative posture while we ship a fix. We can automate that pin for you if you prefer.

Open items still in flight:
- Aegis memory-aware kernel rewrite (owner: infra, ETA 3 weeks).
- Post-deployment verification runbook (owner: reliability team, ETA 2 weeks).

If helpful, we can do a 30-minute technical review with your engineering team next week to go over logs and the timeline. Let me know availability.

Apologies again for the impact. We're treating this with high priority and appreciate your partnership.

Warmly,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
